extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: A training environment for software engineering agents containing 2,438 real-world Python task instances with repository-level codebases, executable runtime environments, unit tests, and natural language task descriptions sourced from GitHub issues and pull requests.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan; Xingyao Wang; Graham Neubig; Navdeep Jaitly; Heng Ji; Alane Suhr; Yizhe Zhang
extraction.citeAs: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang. Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym. Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by identifying Python GitHub repositories using SEART GitHub search, extracting task instances with SWE-Bench's instance extraction script from pull requests and GitHub issues, associating instances with versions, semi-automatically collecting version information, manually configuring executable environments and dependencies for selected repositories, and validating instances with execution-based scripts before filtering failed instances.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data came from real-world GitHub issues, pull requests, repository snapshots, unit tests, configuration files, CI scripts, documentation, and repository metadata from Python repositories. The authors also release SWE-Gym Raw with 64,689 Python GitHub issues spanning 358 repositories without executable environments.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Repositories were selected from those created before 2022-07-01.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors associated instances with version numbers, set up environments version-by-version, semi-automatically collected versions from repository files and tags, manually configured dependencies, validated gold patches with execution-based scripts, filtered out failed instances, and created a Lite subset by excluding tasks based on file-edit count, problem description quality, patch complexity, and error-message-focused tests.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing included converting repositories into task instances, versioning instances, configuring executable environments with pre-installed dependencies using repository configuration files, CI scripts, and documentation, validating that gold patches pass more unit tests than original code, filtering failed instances, and constructing a Lite subset with additional filtering criteria.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human effort was used to manually configure dependencies and executable environments for task instances; annotations were done by a subset of the authors. Expert-written or expert-validated tests serve as validation/reward signals.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Instances were validated by checking that the human gold patch passes more unit tests than the original code, and failed instances were filtered out.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations were done by a subset of the authors.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SWE-Bench instance extraction script; SWE-Bench versioning script; SWE-Bench execution-based validation script; SEART GitHub search
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that improved automated software engineering could increase developer productivity and accessibility, support open-source infrastructure, and make software development more accessible. It also notes possible impacts on software engineering jobs, code ownership, licensing, attribution, and potential misuse for malicious code, calling for responsible deployment considering security, safety, and economic impacts.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset has a long-tail distribution across repositories, with pandas comprising nearly one-third of tasks and bokeh about one percent. The authors also warn that ignoring executable environments could introduce distribution bias. For training trajectories, repeated sampling introduces bias toward easier tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited in environment diversity, including number of repositories, types of tasks, and programming languages. SWE-Gym Raw lacks executable environments and guarantees that unit tests effectively evaluate correctness. The paper also notes that SWE-Gym tasks may be harder than SWE-Bench and include sophisticated repositories, and current settings focus only on task completion rather than human-in-the-loop collaboration.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training software engineering agents and verifier/reward models, evaluating agent performance, enabling inference-time scaling through reranking sampled trajectories, rapid prototyping with SWE-Gym Lite, and supporting future research in SWE agent development and automatic dataset synthesis.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: First, improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer’s productivity and accessibility across industries. ... they can support critical open-source infrastructure and potentially make software development more accessible. Secondly, as these agents become more capable, they may impact software engineering jobs and require careful consideration around code ownership, licensing, and attribution. Additionally, while we focus on legitimate software engineering tasks, similar techniques could potentially be misused to automate the creation of malicious code. We encourage future work to further explore frameworks for responsible deployment of software engineering agents, including considerations around security, safety, and economic impacts.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: SWE-Gym, while effective, is limited by its environment diversity, including the number of repositories, types of tasks, and programming languages. ... While SWE-Gym Raw instances contain code, issue descriptions, and the solution, they do not contain executable environments or a guarantee that its unit tests are effective in evaluating the correctness of a solution. ... Our analysis suggests that tasks in SWE-Gym are on average harder than those included in SWE-Bench. ... Current SWE settings focus solely on task completion, neglecting human-in-the-loop collaboration
